The RGBlimp is a miniature robotic blimp that combines the desirable features of a robotic blimp and a fixed-wing glider.
The RGBlimp uses a helium-filled envelope for buoyant lift and a pair of wings for aerodynamic lift, along with a moving mass for attitude control.
The dynamic model of the RGBlimp considers the dynamic effects of the moving mass, which is often ignored in conventional robotic blimp models.
The authors used nonlinear regression on steady flight experimental data to identify the aerodynamic force and moment coefficients as polynomial functions of the angle of attack and sideslip angle.
The RGBlimp prototype had a total net weight of 6.85 grams, with a stationary mass of 104.81 grams and a moving mass (gondola) of 54.08 grams.
In the steady straight-line flight experiments, the angle of attack α ranged from -20 to 20 degrees, while the sideslip angle β was approximately 0 degrees.
In the steady spiral flight experiments, the angle of attack α ranged from -30 to 30 degrees, and the sideslip angle β ranged from -20 to 20 degrees.
The Reynolds number of the RGBlimp prototype during the experiments was approximately 3.4 × 10^4.
The experiments showed that the RGBlimp prototype with fixed wings had a significantly higher lift-to-drag ratio compared to a conventional robotic blimp without wings.
The proposed dynamic model of the RGBlimp provided better predictions of the dynamic flight behavior compared to the commonly-used model that ignores the Coriolis and centrifugal forces.

The steady spiral flight experiments demonstrated that the RGBlimp could achieve stable spiraling motion by adjusting the moving mass position and the differential thrust between the left and right propellers.
The experimental results of the RGBlimp's dynamic flight matched well with the predictions from the derived dynamic model, validating the modeling approach.
The RGBlimp design is expected to benefit not only the aerodynamic efficiency but also the aerodynamic stability of the robot.
The authors conducted extensive steady flight experiments in a motion capture arena to identify the aerodynamic coefficients of the RGBlimp prototype.
The RGBlimp's fixed wings significantly improved its gliding performance, with a higher lift-to-drag ratio compared to the blimp without wings.
